# White House Press Q&A (Video Lesson)

**目錄：** [Summary](#summary) · [Conversation](#conversation) · [Corrections](#corrections) · [New vocabulary](#new-vocabulary) · [Phrases of the day](#phrases-of-the-day)

**Date:** 2026-11-04
**Type:** 2 Video lesson
**Source:** [選前 11 天，川普 10 分鐘連嗆 CNN、NBC 兩家記者｜白宮記者問答・中英字幕](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c3x01oFw3yc), MJ English, about 10 minutes. Full captions (auto-generated): [captions/2026-11-04-white-house-press-qa-video.txt](../captions/2026-11-04-white-house-press-qa-video.txt)

## Summary
We used a ten-minute White House press Q&A video as a lesson. The captions were auto-generated, so I flagged wrong names such as "Starling" for Starlink. We looked at how a speaker avoids a question ("I wouldn't tell you if I did know") and how a speaker asks "Who are you with?" to a reporter. The political part (gridlock and veto) was too hard, so we switched to the part about protecting "geniuses", where I practiced giving an opinion with "because" and an example. We stopped after Question 3; Question 4 was aborted and is not counted.

**中文摘要:** 我們用一支約十分鐘的白宮記者問答影片當教材。字幕是自動產生的，所以我標出了錯誤的名字，例如把 Starlink 寫成 "Starling"。我們看了講者如何迴避問題（"I wouldn't tell you if I did know"），以及他如何問記者 "Who are you with?"。政治的部分（gridlock、veto）太難，所以改看「保護天才」那一段，練習用 "because" 加上例子說明自己的看法。我們在問題 3 之後停下；問題 4 取消，不計入題數。

## Corrections
| Original | Corrected | Note |
|----------|-----------|------|
| the 記者's question | the **reporter's** question | "記者" is "reporter". 「記者」英文是 reporter。 |
| also ask back | **and** he **asked** the reporter **back** | Add a subject and use the past tense. 要有主詞並用過去式。 |
| who is the 記者 | who **the reporter was** | In an indirect question, do not flip the word order. 間接問句不倒裝。 |
| where're u from | where **they were** from | Write "you" in full in writing; use "they" for one reporter. 書寫時不要用 u；指單一記者可用 they。 |
| donald trump ask | **Donald Trump asked** | Capitalize names and use the past tense. 人名大寫、用過去式。 |
| the reporter answer they are CNN | the reporter **answered that they were with CNN** | Past tense; a person is "with" or "from" CNN, not "CNN". 人是 with / from CNN，不是 CNN。 |
| he just didn't answer that Starlink question | he just **didn't want to answer** that Starlink question | "Didn't answer" is a fact; "didn't want to" is the intention. 一個是事實，一個是意圖。 |
| question, CNN is not the problem | question**.** CNN **isn't** the problem | A comma cannot join two full sentences; use a period, "so" or "because". 逗號不能連接兩個完整句子。 |
| I dont get it | I **don't** get it | Write the apostrophe in "don't". don't 要有撇號。 |
| too much 政治議題 | **too political** | Say "too political" or "too many political topics". 說 too political 或 too many political topics。 |
| there's so many other things need to be protected | **there are** so many other things **that need** to be protected | Plural noun → "there are"; add "that" before "need". 複數用 there are，need 前面加 that。 |
| geniuses is not the must | geniuses **aren't a top priority** | "The must" is not natural; use "a priority". Plural subject → "are". must 當名詞不自然；複數主詞用 are。 |
| It had so many children | **There are** so many children | Use "There are" for "there exist". 「有很多……」用 There are。 |
| hungered or sicked | **hungry** or **sick** | Use adjectives after "are"; "sicked" does not exist. be 後面用形容詞，sicked 不存在。 |
| children that | children **who** | Use "who" for people. 指人用 who。 |
| they're need helped first | **they need to be helped** first / **they need help** first | "They're" = "they are", so it cannot go before "need"; use the passive or "need help". they're 後面不能接 need。 |

## New vocabulary
- **reporter** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=reporter&op=translate)): a person who asks questions and writes or speaks news for a news organization (記者) — The reporter asked the president a difficult question.
- **Who are you with?** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=Who%20are%20you%20with%3F&op=translate)): which news organization or company do you work for? (你是哪一家媒體／公司的？) — "Who are you with?" "I'm with a local newspaper."
- **I wouldn't tell you if I did know.** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=I%20wouldn%27t%20tell%20you%20if%20I%20did%20know&op=translate)): I know, or maybe I don't, but I would not say it either way (就算我知道，我也不會告訴你) — I wouldn't tell you if I did know where the party is.
- **We have all the cards.** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=We%20have%20all%20the%20cards&op=translate)): we have the stronger position in a negotiation (我們握有所有的牌，占上風) — In this deal, we have all the cards.
- **gridlock** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=gridlock&op=translate)): a situation where nothing can move or be decided, such as in politics (僵局) — Political gridlock stopped the new law.
- **veto** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=veto&op=translate)): to officially refuse to approve a law or decision (否決) — The president threatened to veto the bill.
- **stalemate** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=stalemate&op=translate)): a situation where neither side can win or make progress (僵持) — The talks ended in a stalemate.
- **sticking point** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=sticking%20point&op=translate)): a part of a discussion that is hard to agree on (卡關的爭議點) — Price was the main sticking point in the deal.
- **wither** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=wither&op=translate)): to become weak and slowly die or fade (枯萎、慢慢衰弱) — Without water, the plant started to wither.
- **backlash** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=backlash&op=translate)): a strong negative reaction from many people (反彈) — The new rule caused a public backlash.
- **midterm** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=midterm&op=translate)): an election held in the middle of a president's term; also an exam in the middle of a course (期中選舉；期中考) — The midterm election is in November.
- **brilliant** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=brilliant&op=translate)): very clever or talented (非常聰明的、傑出的) — She is a brilliant scientist.
- **genius** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=genius&op=translate)): a person with extraordinary intelligence or talent (天才) — Many people called him a genius.
- **obligation** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=obligation&op=translate)): something you must do because it is right or required (義務、責任) — We have an obligation to help children in need.
- **priority** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=priority&op=translate)): something that is more important than other things (優先事項) — Safety is our top priority.
- **First things first.** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=First%20things%20first&op=translate)): do the most important thing before anything else (先做最重要的事) — First things first, let's eat, then we'll talk.
- **I don't get it.** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=I%20don%27t%20get%20it&op=translate)): I don't understand (我不懂) — I don't get it. Can you explain again?
- **hungry** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=hungry&op=translate)): needing food (餓的) — Many children in the world are still hungry.
- **starving** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=starving&op=translate)): extremely hungry, or dying from lack of food (快餓死的) — I'm starving, let's order pizza.
- **in need** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=in%20need&op=translate)): without enough food, money or help (需要幫助的) — We donate clothes to children in need.

## Phrases of the day
### 1. **Who are you with?** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=Who%20are%20you%20with%3F&op=translate))
- **Meaning:** which news organization or company do you work for? (你是哪一家媒體／公司的？)
- **Tone:** casual
- **Examples:**
  - "Who are you with?" "I'm with a local newspaper."
    → 「你是哪家媒體的？」「我是地方報社的。」
  - Who are you with? I don't think I've seen you at this event.
    → 你是哪個單位的？我好像沒在這個活動看過你。
  - Reporters at the door are usually asked, "Who are you with?"
    → 門口的記者通常會被問：「你是哪家媒體的？」
- **Similar expressions:** who you with (said by the speaker), who are you here with (你是跟誰一起來的)
- **Source:** from this conversation (you learned it in Question 1 and wrote "with CNN")

### 4. **I wouldn't tell you if I did know.** ([Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/?sl=en&tl=zh-TW&text=I%20wouldn%27t%20tell%20you%20if%20I%20did%20know&op=translate))
